statement: A gain of 0.01 on the primary metric's own scale (baseline.MIN_GAIN) is the smallest gain that matters for every task, including the mean squared error of a numeric outcome in its squared outcome units, log loss in nats, the ranked probability score and the Brier score at a horizon, so a gain below 0.01 is 'too small to matter whatever the folds say'.
regime: Prediction; every task; the verdict reads PRIMARY[task] (regression: mse, binary/multiclass: log_loss, ordinal: rps, time to event: brier_t)
decision: The 'better' threshold in the baseline verdict; also the equivalence margin δ = MIN_GAIN/2 of the T1 nested-tuning test and the STRATIFICATION_OPTIMISM argument
user_sees: "Better than the outcome's average by too little to matter: CV MSE 101.2 against 101.3, a gain of 0.009 (95% interval 0.002 to 0.016), under 0.01."
claimed_basis: 'a convention, not a cited rule' (baseline.py:25-27); STRATIFICATION_OPTIMISM §5 and RECIPES §8 T1 reuse it as 'the app's smallest meaningful gain'.
notes: [part id F2-002] LIKELY WRONG for regression: the docstring was written for R² (scale-free), but since MS6 the regression primary is the MSE, whose scale is the outcome's units squared, so 0.01 is negligible for glucose in mg/dL (variance ~400) and the whole variance for an outcome on a 0–1 scale. For log loss 0.01 nats is a substantive but scale-free choice. The tolerance basis string shown to users says 'at least 0.01 (a convention)'.

statement: For tuning XGBoost under prediction, the search box learning rate [0.01, 0.3] (log), depth [2, 10], min child weight [1, 64] rows-equivalent (log), row share [0.5, 1], column share per tree [0.3, 1], L2 λ [1e-3, 100] (log), rounds [25, 1,000] (only without early stopping), with α=0, tree booster and hist fixed, contains the well-performing settings.
decision: XGBoost's declared search space and fixed settings
user_sees: Tuning line and Settings table as for boosted trees; reason "Its settings are searched inside every training fold, with XGBoost's defaults always among the candidates."
claimed_basis: Probst, Boulesteix & Bischl 2019 (λ 2^[−10, 10]; child weight 2^[0, 7]); Chen & Guestrin 2016 / XGBoost tuning notes; RECIPES §4.1 ("conventions, narrowed").
notes: [part id F4-004] Ranges are narrowed from the cited ones (λ capped at 100 vs 2^10≈1024; child weight 64 vs 128). Linear booster excluded because it "treats missing values as zeros" (RECIPES §2.2) and scale_pos_weight excluded because reweighting goes through the imbalance lever, which recalibrates (RECIPES §2.2, §7.3) — both stated as 'impossible by construction'.

statement: Multiple imputation with the outcome in the imputation model is invalid under prediction, because a held-out row's own outcome would fill its predictors and a new row has none; under prediction blanks must be filled in each training fold without the outcome.
regime: prediction, missing predictor values, strategy = multiple_imputation
decision: refusal of multiple imputation under prediction, with in-fold fill and complete cases as exits
user_sees: "Multiple imputation puts the outcome in the imputation model. That is right for inference, but a prediction model must impute a new row without its outcome, so under prediction the imputation is f...
claimed_basis: Sisk et al. 2023; BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 4; audit WP7, ME-01.
notes: [part id F5-037] turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp7_missing_data.py::test_1_multiple_imputation_with_the_outcome_is_refused_under_prediction pins the refusal. MI without the outcome fitted in-fold would avoid the stated problem but is not offered either. Inference-side missing-data refusals in the same validator are out of area A.

statement: A column named as a percent of energy whose values all lie at or below 1 holds fractions rather than percentages, and values outside 0–100 are not percentages of energy, so either is refused before a percent-of-energy swap.
regime: percent-of-energy columns moved by a share swap
decision: whether the share swap can be computed
user_sees: fat_pct_kcal reads as a percent of energy, but every value is at most 1: it holds fractions, so a 5-point step would be 500% of energy.
notes: A genuine percent column whose values are all ≤ 1 (e.g. alcohol's share in a low-drinking sample) would be refused. test_wp12a::test_b24_shares_are_never_moved_in_kcal_and_fractions_are_refused checks the refusal only.

statement: Complete-case analysis gives unbiased regression coefficients if and only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors.
regime: inference; complete-case analysis of a regression (linear, logistic, Cox, etc.) with missing predictors
decision: complete-cases option (available, ranked second under inference); its stated assumption in the record and methods sentence; the row-loss concern
user_sees: complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010)
notes: Partial: the complete-case arm checks only the sufficiency direction in one linear scenario (missingness depends on the exposure). The option label (missing.py:139) says 'Sound if ...' (sufficient) while COMPLETE_CASE_ASSUMPTION and row_loss_concern (missing.py:1763-1764: 'estimate without bias only if') assert necessity; for logistic-regression odds ratios complete cases are also unbiased when missingness depends on the outcome alone, so 'only if' may be overstated for binary outcomes.

statement: GEE intervals in a cluster trial use t on the number of clusters minus the number of cluster-level terms (intercept, arm and any covariate constant within clusters), i.e. K − 2 for two arms and no cluster-level covariate.
user_sees: t on the clusters less the cluster-level terms (12 − 3 = 9)

statement: When the Newton fit drives a coefficient beyond 20 SDs of its column on the log-hazard scale (or does not converge), the partial likelihood has no finite maximum (monotone likelihood, 'in one of its groups every row has the event, or none does'), so the hazard ratio is infinite and no interval or p-value is reported.
user_sees: The partial likelihood has no maximum for `x` (in one of its groups every row has the event, or none does), so the hazard ratio is infinite and no interval or p-value is reported.
claimed_basis: none stated (survival.py:59: 'a log hazard ratio of 20 per SD is an infinite one')
notes: Monotone likelihood in Cox arises when a covariate orders the risk sets perfectly (e.g. a group with no events); a group where every row has the event does not by itself make it monotone, and non-convergence for other reasons gets the same message. Also survival.py:573-581.

statement: The between-site heterogeneity of a prediction model's performance is better conveyed by a 95% prediction interval for a new site, μ̂ ± t(k-2)·√(τ̂² + σ̂_μ²), than by I² (which can mislead when site sizes are large), so the prediction interval is said first, and it needs at least three sites.
user_sees: "in a new site it would lie between ... and ... (95% prediction interval), I² ..."
claimed_basis: Riley et al. 2016 (BMJ 353:i3140); Higgins, Thompson & Spiegelhalter 2009
notes: Docstring :37-43. The test checks the PI formula against metafor predtype='Riley' (computation), not the 'better than I²' claim.

statement: Two roles that remove a column from the predictors cannot be settled by values: free text (a category with many labels such as country of birth, ~70 labels, or a text identifier fits the same label count) and survey-design part (a measurement with positive values, or a group code that is a predictor, fits the same); each needs the user's confirmation.
regime: Text columns with many labels; columns read as survey weight, stratum or PSU.
decision: Free-text or design role (left out of the model) vs predictor.
user_sees: Asked on the roles card; the column stays a predictor candidate until confirmed.
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14.3 (fourth gate: 'a label count read as free text (country of birth has 70)').
notes: role:design at readings.py:1125. test_discriminate.py::test_b7 / ::test_a6 check behavior (a 70-label category is asked, never dropped). | Inventory source id: F3-007.

statement: A column named like an identifier is not a unit identifier (and clustering intervals by it is invalid) when it holds fewer than 3 distinct values, or at most 10 repeating word labels without digits (e.g., a case-control `patient` 0/1, `respondent` Self/Proxy, `person` mother/father); 3-10 repeating coded values may be a small study's units or a group code and are asked; more than 10 repeating values, or one value per row, is a unit structure.
regime: Any table; columns whose names read as identifiers.
decision: Identifier role confidence and whether it may cluster intervals or group the seal.
user_sees: "it holds only `2` values (`0`, `1`), a category's labels, not units"
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14 rule 1: "An identifier has at least 3 distinct values and a unit structure." (gate: `participant` coded yes/no clustered intervals by 2 values, so no interval was reported); FEW_UNITS = CATEGORY_LEVELS 10 (recognizers.py:1412-1425).
notes: Repeating word labels with more than 10 levels are 'few' (asked, never high). test_recognition_leash.py::test_a2_the_case_control_inference_never_clusters_by_a_category checks behavior. | Inventory source id: F3-038.

statement: A feature whose D-ratio (pooled-QC SD over the study samples' SD) is 50% or more carries too little biological variance relative to technical variance and is removed, with the QC SD frozen before the seal and the study SD taken from each training fold.
regime: metabolomics; pooled-QC answer variant with D-ratio chosen
user_sees: "Within each training fold, features whose D-ratio (QC over study-sample standard deviation) was 50% or more were removed."
claimed_basis: Broadhurst et al. 2018: 'the acceptance criterion for D-ratio is set to, at most, < 50%'.
notes: Constant D_RATIO_MAX at qc_drift.py:59. A feature without a QC SD is kept. Offered as an option variant, not a default for every run. | Inventory source id: F5-030.

statement: Under prediction, internal validation must resample the entire modeling pipeline, so every step learned from data (energy-adjustment residuals, scaling, imputation, PCA loadings, feature ranking and selection, thresholds, tuning) is fit inside each training fold; selecting features on all samples can report near-zero error when no signal exists.
regime: prediction; any table; cross-validation or bootstrap
decision: the fit pipeline (every learned step in-fold) and the split drawers
user_sees: Internal validation must resample the entire modeling pipeline: imputation, transformation, selection and tuning.
claimed_basis: CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK §A5.5 (SETTLED); GENOMICS_PACK §08 (Ambroise & McLachlan 2002); WHAT_EXPLORATION_MAY_DECIDE §5.3 (Hornung 2015; Moscovich & Rosset 2022)
notes: Also content.py:471-475, 1009-1013 (near-zero error), 1132-1136 ('fitting it on all rows before cross-validation leaks the held-out rows into every fold'), 1363-1367. Under inference the app fits outcome-free steps on all rows (WHAT_EXPLORATION row 1), consistent with this being a prediction rule.

statement: A TNTC ('too numerous to count') plate count is right-censored above the countable range (15–300 colonies per plate in FDA's BAM, 2026 edition), not missing, whereas QNS or a hemolyzed specimen is a measurement failure with no value and is treated as missing.
regime: clinical lens; microbiology and lab results
decision: TNTC kept as censored rather than routed to missing
user_sees: TNTC, too numerous to count, means a plate held more colonies than its countable range, 15–300 per plate in FDA's Bacteriological Analytical Manual (2026 edition)
notes: Also finding_words.py:224-306. test_wp15_claims.py::test_4_tntc_* check the text. A hemolyzed specimen can still give values for some analytes.

statement: Values filled before the table was made by an unrecorded method are read as missing and re-imputed in each training fold at the median without indicators, because their missingness belongs to the upstream process, not the person, and does not exist at the moment of use.
regime: prediction; provider-imputed values flagged in the table
user_sees: "Read them as missing" (Recommended): "Each is filled again in each training fold, from the other people's values and never from glucose."
notes: Beat D (lines 272-346). If the upstream filling depended on the person (e.g., a cuff failing on large arms), the missingness is informative about the person.

statement: Views that never use the outcome may shape the representation (transforms, knots, filters, imputation rules), and under inference steps learned without the outcome may be fit on the full analysis sample; views that use the outcome may only add candidates to a declared search under prediction (never prune it) and under inference are reported, not acted on, unless a declared selection-aware method carries them.
regime: exploration (First look and Explore) across purposes
decision: what an exploration thread may feed (enforced at registration)
claimed_basis: Harrell RMS 4.7; Baillie 2022; Gelman & Loken 2013; Belloni et al. 2014; Ambroise & McLachlan 2002
notes: UNDERSTANDING_LAYER.md §0 item 5 (enforced when a thread registers). §1 also requires each rule to be declared before the data judge it, rerun in every resample, and its uncertainty carried.
